summary: First iteration end-to-end testing of Qwebliq platform. Wrote pytest suite (19 tests) covering public content, calculator, inquiry, newsletter, auth guards, admin overview/inquiries/publishing, and admin-created client login + client portal. Wrote Playwright UI test hitting the external preview URL covering home rendering, calculator, FAQ search, inquiry+newsletter submission, admin login and auth protection, admin publishing (feed, client), client portal, and mobile 390px layout. Fixed 2 backend 500-error bugs (ObjectId leaking in POST response bodies) that were blocking admin project/feed/blog/client creation. After fix, backend 19/19 pass and full UI journey succeeds including admin-created client sign-in.

minor.issue: Returns 401 on public pages because AuthContext eagerly probes session at mount (expected but produces console noise on every anonymous page load)

ui_bugs.issue: React 'Encountered two children with the same key' warning because feed posts use post.title as key; when admin publishes duplicate titles (or seeded+new match) React throws duplicate-key warning. Use unique id/created_at instead.

issues: When the mobile nav (nav-links.nav-open) is opened, background is transparent — hero heading 'Building digital experiences that move businesses.' visibly bleeds through the menu. Add a solid/opaque background or backdrop to the open mobile drawer.

Contact block still uses the placeholder copy 'Contact details are ready to be tailored…' and WhatsApp CTA href='https://wa.me/' has no number — flagged as intentional editable placeholder per requirements, but WhatsApp link currently leads to an invalid destination.

action_items: Use a stable unique key (e.g. post._id / post.title+date) when mapping feed posts in HomePage.jsx to remove React duplicate-key warning.
Give the open mobile navigation drawer a solid background (or backdrop) so page content does not show through at 390px.
Populate the WhatsApp CTA href with a real number when contact details are finalised (currently 'https://wa.me/').
Consider suppressing /api/auth/me probe (or handling 401 silently) for anonymous visitors to reduce console noise on the public homepage.
critical_code_review_comments: FIXED: /api/admin/projects, /api/admin/feed, /api/admin/blog, /api/auth/clients returned 500 because motor's insert_one mutates the passed dict with an ObjectId `_id`; FastAPI could not serialize it. Added document.pop('_id', None) before returning.
auth.py refresh handler uses __import__('os').environ['JWT_SECRET'] — should import os at top of file for clarity.
public.py newsletter handler swallows any exception whose message doesn't contain 'duplicate'; should catch pymongo DuplicateKeyError explicitly rather than string-match.
security.get_current_user catches jwt.InvalidTokenError but on ObjectId parse failure will also raise bson.errors.InvalidId which is not in the except tuple — will surface as 500 instead of 401.

database.seed_application_data reseeds bcrypt hash every startup when password matches by re-hashing — hash comparison is done, but existing_admin path recomputes password_hash string that isn't used (minor waste).
Login rate limit stores {ip:email} identifier so an attacker rotating emails from same IP can bypass lockout; consider per-IP counter too.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of critical flows (home, calculator, FAQ, inquiry, newsletter, auth guard, admin login+publish+create client, client portal login, mobile layout)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend suite lives at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py and runs against REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (external preview URL). All admin publishing endpoints previously returned 500 due to ObjectId in response body — fixed in this iteration by popping _id after insert_one. If future features add more POST endpoints returning inserted docs, apply same pattern. AuthContext hits /api/auth/me eagerly, so 401s in the console on public pages are expected. Mobile drawer background transparency and feed React key uniqueness are outstanding UI-side items for main agent.
rca of the issue: Motor's AsyncIOMotorCollection.insert_one mutates the dict argument in place, injecting the newly generated ObjectId under key '_id'. The admin endpoints in dashboard.py and the client creation endpoint in auth.py assigned document['id'] = str(result.inserted_id) but returned the same dict — still containing the raw ObjectId under '_id'. FastAPI's default response serializer (pydantic) cannot serialize bson ObjectId, raising PydanticSerializationError and yielding HTTP 500. Reproduction: POST /api/admin/projects (or /feed, /blog, /auth/clients) with a valid admin cookie and valid payload -> 500 Internal Server Error. Fix: pop '_id' from the document before returning, keeping the string 'id' field. Verified by re-running backend_test.py (19/19 pass) and by full UI journey (admin publishes feed + creates client via Studio publishing tabs, client subsequently signs in and reaches /client portal).
